deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page contains no worked derivation and no displayed equation. It is combinatorial bookkeeping. Riemann writes lists of linear combinations of Abel-integral values of points; I read these as the arguments of theta functions ϑ(…) of genus p. He also writes lists of letter-tuples, which look like selections of p points. Both serve the theta-function work on the previous page.

Context from the previous page. There the case p=6 is set up with point groups a, a', b, b' (the overset counts 6, 8, 5, … appear to be group sizes). Riemann writes ϑ(a+Σa+Σb'), ϑ(a'+Σa), ϑ(b'_1+Σa) and so on. Here a letter stands for u(a), the vector of Abelian integrals at a point, and Σa stands for Σ u over a whole group. He then writes an alternating sum and an identity of products:
- Σ ± Π ϑ(a+Σa+Σb') · Π_{a'} ϑ(a'+Σa) = (quotients of products Π_ν^3 ϑ(… + Σb + Σa^ν − Σb^ν)) · Π ϑ(b+Σa+Σb').
- ϑ(b'_1+Σa) Π_ν^3 ϑ(b'_1+Σb+Σa^ν−Σb^ν) = Π_ν^3 ϑ(a'+Σb+Σa^ν−Σb^ν) ϑ(a'+Σa).
This has the shape of a theta-function generalization of a Cauchy determinant: a determinant of theta quotients evaluated as a product. Riemann's vanishing theorem decides which products are non-zero.

The next page carries a draft rental letter dated May–September 1864 and the vanishing condition 'Wenn ϑ(v)=0 und ϑ(α−u+v) nicht identisch null'. Together with the address line on this page, 'Pisa. Via della Maddalena 25', this dates the sheet to Riemann's stay in Pisa in spring 1864.

Block 1 (top). Two groups a, b and their primed partners a', b'. For a point x of each group the argument is:
- x ∈ a: a+Σa+Σb'
- x ∈ a': a'+Σa'+Σa
- x ∈ b: b+Σb'+Σa
- x ∈ b': b'+Σa'+Σa
So each point is shifted by the sum of its own (or its partner's) group plus a fixed background Σa. He then specializes by singling out points b'_1, a'_1, b'_2: 'b'_1+Σb'_1+Σa', 'b'_2+Σb'+Σa'. A crossed-out attempt reads a+Σa+b'_1+Σb', a'_1+a'+Σa'+Σa, Σb'+Σa. This tracks how arguments change when one point is moved from one group to another, which is the step in an induction or row expansion of the determinant.

Block 2. Points a_1, a_2 are successively removed from the a-group. Σ_1 a, Σ_{12} a, Σ_2 a, Σ_3 a denote partial sums with indices omitted. The arguments become:
- a'+Σa'+a_1+Σa, then a'+Σa'+a_1+a_2+Σ_2a
- a+Σ_1a+a_1+Σb', then a+Σ_2a+a_1+a_2+Σb'
- Σa+Σb'+a_1, then Σa+Σb'+a_1+a_2
- a_1+Σa+Σ_2a+Σa', then a_1+a_2+Σ_3a+Σa'
This is bookkeeping for an inductive step (p → p−1, or n → n+1 points).

Block 3. Three-level version with groups a, a', a'' and b, b', b'':
- b+Σb'+Σb''+Σa, b'+Σa'+Σb''+Σa, b''+Σa''+Σb'+Σa
- a'+Σa'+Σb''+Σa, a''+Σa''+(Σa?)+Σb', a+Σa+Σb'+Σb''
This generalizes block 1 to more groups.

Block 4 (after the address). Three and four groups a, b, c, d.
- Triangular scheme: a+Σa'+Σb'+Σc', b+Σa+Σb'+Σc', with c, d left blank.
- Diagonal scheme: a+Σa'+Σb+Σc, b+Σa+Σb'+Σc, c+Σa+Σb+Σc', d+Σa+Σb+Σc.
  Rule (my formulation): for x in group g the argument is x plus the sum of all groups, with group g replaced by its primed partner.
- Mixed forms where one group is replaced by individual points d_1, d_2, d_3: a'+b+c+Σd_3, c'+Σa+b+d_2, b'+Σa+c+d_3, d_3+Σa+b+c+d_1+d_2, a+Σa'+b+c+Σd_3, and so on. Here Σd_k presumably means the d-sum with d_k omitted.

Block 5 (lower half). Lists of 5-letter (and some 6-letter) tuples: abc a'_1a'_2, abc d_1a'_1, abc d_1a'_2, bc d_1a'_1a'_2, abc d_1d_2, a'_1bc d_1d_2, b'ac d'_1d'_2, ab c' a'_1 d_1, …, ac d_1 a'_1, and so on. Some are bracketed into columns and some are joined by a loop. My interpretation: these enumerate which sets of points make up the divisor in each theta argument, i.e. the terms of an expansion. Riemann seems to be checking which terms survive by the vanishing theorem, ϑ(Σ_{p points} u − Σ … ) = 0 when the points are special. They may also be the minors appearing in a Laplace expansion.

I cannot reconstruct the final identity from this page alone. The page records the indexing scheme only.
errors: No equations are asserted on this page, so nothing can be checked for correctness; only patterns of arguments are listed.

In block 3 the term transcribed 'a''+Σa''+Σa''+Σb'' repeats Σa''. By the pattern of the neighbouring entries it should probably be a''+Σa''+Σa+Σb' (or +Σa'). This is either a slip by Riemann or a misreading.
Several entries are struck through (the a+Σa+b'_1+Σb' line, the a_1,Σa',c line, the a'_1 b c line, abc d'_1d'_2). These are abandoned attempts, not results.

results.what: Systematic table of theta arguments x + Σ(groups, with x's own group replaced by its primed partner). This is the indexing for a determinant/product identity for genus-p theta functions with several point groups, continuing the previous page's Σ±Πϑ = Πϑ identity.
results.modern_name: Theta-function analogue of the Cauchy determinant (Frobenius determinant formula; Fay's identity, corollary 2.19 of Fay 1973), together with Riemann's vanishing theorem.
results.usually_credited_to: Frobenius (1882, elliptic case); J. Fay, Theta Functions on Riemann Surfaces (1973), higher genus.

results.what: Inductive bookkeeping of how theta arguments change when single points a_1, a_2 are removed from a group (partial sums Σ_1a, Σ_12a, Σ_2a, Σ_3a).
results.modern_name: Induction step / Laplace expansion in a theta determinant identity.

results.what: Enumeration of p-element point subsets (abc a'_1a'_2, abc d_1d_2, …) to decide which theta products vanish.
results.modern_name: Application of the Riemann vanishing theorem / special divisors.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1865, Über das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen)

results.what: Address 'Pisa, Via della Maddalena 25' and the adjacent rental draft date the sheet to spring 1864.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is only index bookkeeping. With the previous page, though, it suggests Riemann was working in 1864 on multi-group theta product/determinant identities in genus p, of the type later associated with Frobenius and Fay. That is a notable unpublished direction. However, no identity is stated or provable from this page, so the evidence is weak.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; x1,x2,x3,y1,y2,y3=symbols('x1 x2 x3 y1 y2 y3'); X=[x1,x2,x3]; Y=[y1,y2,y3]; M=Matrix(3,3,lambda i,j:1/(X[i]-Y[j])); simplify(M.det() - prod([(X[j]-X[i])*(Y[i]-Y[j]) for i in range(3) for j in range(i+1,3)])/prod([X[i]-Y[j] for i in range(3) for j in range(3)]))
checkable.asserts: Genus-0 (Cauchy) case of the determinant-equals-product identity whose theta analogue the page's argument tables appear to index; should simplify to 0.
Number of 5-point subsets of the 7 symbols occurring in the lower lists (21). Riemann lists only a selection, presumably those not killed by vanishing.
